title: Observers, systems and commands that use closures and panic require explicit return type after Rust 2024 edition

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
As discussed [on Discord](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/1354184220263841812/1359585787846328441) with @participant7, this is due to Rust 2024, and is not our bug. It's arguably not a bug at all!

See https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2024/never-type-fallback.html for the context on this change, which recommends the same workaround of explicitly specifying the return type. The same code will compile just fine as functions rather than closures, because the return type of functions is never inferred (even if it's defaulted to ()).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
From `Gl` [on Discord](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/691052431974465548/1359680140975542313).

>If we _desperately_ need this, there's actually a way to get never-types to work in stable Rust, using associated types 

```rs
type Never = <u8 as TryFrom<u8>>::Error;
```
> this leverages the fact that there's a blanket impl for `TryFrom<T>` for `T` where Error is defined as `!`

And, that does indeed work: https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=77fbd787405712a153404ca23d5d0263

There may need to be a bit of shenanigans to avoid conflicting impls, but we should be able to get that working here. I'm going to check upstream to see if they're okay with us abusing this hole.

https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=922fa8c98bb3023b248870c6a786eb52

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I _was_ able to reframe Observers to share the same `T` output impl by framing our error handler logic as:

```rust
IntoObserverSystem<E: 'static, B: Bundle, M, Out: HandleSystemOut>:
```

This unfortunately is just as shell game, as this observer results in a return type of `!`:

```rust
app.add_observer(|_: Trigger<Thing>| {
    panic!("oh no!");
})
```

And we can't implement `HandleSystemOut` for `!` because `!` is experimental. Worth escalating to the Rust team as this feels intractable.
